name: Poyanáwa
confidence_why: 2 independent first-hand descriptions agree (1 state the same rule, 0 refine it); none contradicts.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: Coding = fixed-dominant final stress (final stress, in the dominant set, not in the strict set). Paula 1992 states four times (pp. 47, 70, 73, 105) that intensity accent is fixed/predictable on the last syllable and non-phonemic; the only deviations are (a) a handful of lexicalised compounds with stress on each root and (b) <=3 tokens like ['taɨ] 'pé' that the author reanalyses as /ay/ diphthongs, i.e. still final. That matches fixed final with in the dominant set; not in the strict set is defensible given the double-stressed compounds (one could even argue counts as exceptionless (the strict set), but no reclassification is warranted). The source is a 1992 fieldwork MA thesis, the sole descriptive reference in Glottolog and, per web search, the only phonological description that exists (language near-dormant, ~1 speaker; later UFAC theses are on schooling/revitalisation). Quote confirmed verbatim on page scan; custody gap closed by downloading the open PD

sources.quote: p.47: 'Em Poyanáwa, a palavra pode ser definida como uma "forma livre mínima" ... marcada por uma acentuação fixa na última sílaba' with exx. [hu'bu] 'fumo', [taka'ra] 'galinha', [ira'bu] 'filho'; apparent compounds keep each root's stress ([taka'ravu'du] 'galo', [ba'ʂibuh'na] 'poeira'), 'apenas um pequeno número desses casos'. p.70: 'O suprassegmento acento de intensidade ... é predizível em Poyanáwa: ocorre na última sílaba do enunciado. A nível lexical o segmento não apresenta oposição ... não se constituindo, portanto, em um fonema da língua.' p.73: 'a palavra será delimitada pelo acento d
